chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: Capone men taking over the Dreamland for the night
summary: He was once in a Dreamland raid, and Capone people closed the club for private nights and tipped the band, who played until sunup.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Were you ever involved in -- was there ever a time in your career, where the mob affected what you did?

Well, no, I don't think they affected, and I was in a raid once in the Dreamland, that's all I remember and nothing happened, you know, money would straighten out everything in those days. But I was in a raid in Chicago, and I remember the Capone -- members of the Capone organization come in all the time. You could tell when they came into a club, cause they were big spenders, and they just practically came in and locked the door and they took charge of the night. You know, they'd close it for the night for their own entertainment.

They were very nice tippers, and the band stayed after hours, they'd come at 3:00 o'clock or 4:00, we'd stay there till sunup, play for them. We came out with quite a nice little pocket-ful of money. During that time.
So they really liked the music?
Oh they did, oh sure, well I think if it wasn't for the Capone organization I don't think the clubs would've existed in Chicago at that time.
